summary: Upstream runtime crashloop tied to rapid small-payload bursts causing elevated API 5xx rate
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC we observed a progressive increase in 5xx responses from API Gateway for a small set of requests from customer Acme Personalization. Impact: customer application experienced ~12-18% error rate (5xx) for short-lived chat and embedding mix requests resulting in failed personalization calls and user-visible failures. Environment: production; traffic originates from Acme's dedicated pool in us-east and also shows correlated spikes in eu-west. Observed behavior: API Gateway returns 502/503 intermittently. Traces show upstream runtime instances hitting short-lived crashloops and the autoscaler performing rapid warms/cools. Expected behavior: steady <0.1% 5xx for this tenant. Additional context: errors cluster during tight burst windows from the customer (small payloads, high QPS), and coincide with runtime worker restarts referencing NVML/GPU driver logs and runtime watchdogs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a client on customer account, send a burst of 40-60 small chat+embedding requests concurrently (payloads <1KB) to /v1/chat/stream
2) Repeat bursts every 30s for 10 minutes to emulate tenant spike profile
3) Observe API Gateway return 502/503 for 10-18% of requests and runtime pod restarts in the same timeframe

comments: 2026-03-10 08:45 - Priya Nair (Support): Customer reported elevated error rate and provided request traces. Initial triage shows upstream restarts. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-10 09:10 - Daniel Park (SRE): Observed correlated runtime watchdog resets; collecting coredumps and nvml logs. Suspect short-lived GPU init failures during rapid scale-up.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Miguel Alvarez (Eng): Reproduced locally with a small burst harness. Found a race in runtime startup where prefetched KV cache is invalidated if model variant swap happens simultaneously. Creating PR to add startup backoff and stronger init checks.

2026-03-11 02:18 - Tom Bennett (Acme): Provided additional timestamps and said the bursts are from a nightly personalization job at 08:30 that was recently scaled. Asking for mitigation while fix is deployed.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Sophie Laurent (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation: rate-limit short-lived high-QPS tenants to 30 rps per-instance during warmup and enabled a 10s init grace window in staging for validation. Monitoring shows 5xx down to ~1.1% for Acme in us-east after mitigation.
investigation_notes: - Pattern: 5xx spikes align with tenant-scale bursts where autoscaler increases replicas quickly from 2->6 within ~30s.
- Runtime logs include 'gpu-watchdog-timeout' then immediate process exit; NVML reports 'UNINITIALIZED' in some restarts suggesting driver init contention under rapid spin-up.
- Kernel: startup race between model hot-swap/prefetch and GPU init path leads to partial state; when next request arrives, runtime panics and exits rather than gracefully failing request.
- Related signals: increased NVMe IO wait noted on nodes concurrently performing snapshotting; potential I/O contention extends GPU init time and amplifies race window.
- Reproduction: local harness reproduced with scripted burst and artificially slowed NVML init (strace sleep on /dev/nv0) resulted in identical crashloop pattern.
- Hypotheses ranked: 1) GPU init race with model swap (high confidence), 2) NVMe snapshot I/O causing init delays (medium), 3) API gateway mis-propagated retries amplifying error rate (low).
resolution: Mitigation applied and code fix in progress. Short-term: implemented per-tenant warmup rate limiting and a 10s startup grace that defers accepting traffic until runtime reports full GPU init and KV cache readiness. Mid-term: merged runtime PR to add deterministic GPU init handshake and serialized model prefetch during startup (PR link above). Long-term: autoscaler change to stagger replica startups and guard against simultaneous model hot-swap across replicas. Customer communicated and patch scheduled for rollout to production 2026-03-14 with follow-up monitoring for 72 hours.
postmortem_followup: - Create an autoscaler policy to jitter replica scale-ups for dedicated pools (owner: infra/autoscaler)
- Add a runtime readiness probe that checks GPU and KV cache readiness before marking pod healthy (owner: serving-runtime)
- Extend observability: per-tenant GPU-init-duration metric and dashboard (owner: observability)
- Run retrospective with customer to validate burst shaping options (owner: CSM)
- Validate NVMe snapshot scheduling to avoid heavy IO during warmup windows (owner: platform-storage)
resolution_status: Partial mitigation deployed; code fix merged to staging; production rollout scheduled
external_communication_notes: Notified customer (Acme Personalization) of temporary mitigation 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC and planned full fix/rollout 2026-03-14. Asked customer to throttle their nightly job as an interim measure if possible.
customer_impact_summary: Acme reported intermittent failures for personalization endpoints during their nightly burst window, impacting ~5% of end-users at peak. Mitigation reduced error rate to ~1% regionally; full fix expected to restore baseline <0.1%.
